para.text: XYGRAPH3D uses standard perspective drawing. This means that a viewing position has to be defined to obtain a result. This viewing position is determined by two directions, a direction in the horizontal plane, and a vertical direction (

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: The direction in the horizontal plane is just opposite that of a normal compass where 0° means North, see figure. So in XYGRAPH3D a direction of 0° means: ‘facing North’, a direction of 90° means ‘facing East’, etc. The result of this is that an orientation of 0° corresponds to the ‘normal’ viewing position as obtained when for example looking to a graph on paper laying on your desk. Also, when looking from above, an increase of this angle results in the rotation of the graph in the conventional positive direction.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

para.text: The height angle of the viewing position is simply the tilt angle. As an example the figure shows a situation of a position (in the xy plane) of 270°, and a height (tilt angle) of 30°. The third parameter is the viewing distance, this determines the amount of perspective in the drawing.

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: Keep in mind that XYGRAPH3D is not a full 3D development code. Those programs have a different way of constructing an image, for example using ray-tracing. XYGRAPH3D is basically intended for the presentation of data.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: A 3D image is simulated by creating quasi-3D objects. The full effect is only obtained if not only these objects but also the different faces of solids (polyhedra) are plotted in the correct order: from back to front! This is automatically done in
, but in all other situations you have to take care of that yourself.
